note: Found on 2026-10-03 in review, by a random run of 40 inversions. A Schlumberger sounding from 3 m that reads 40.6 and then 40.0 ohm-m at the first spacing and about 6 ohm-m from 5 m out. Both engines converged to two layers at the same misfit, with a top layer of 920 ohm-m and 0.702 m in Python and 939 ohm-m and 0.699 m in the browser. It was recorded as an open question of method, a resistivity the data do not determine, but the two searches never started from the same model: at the first spacing the browser's interp returned the first reading where np.interp returns the second, so the browser's starting top layer was 40.6 ohm-m and Python's 40.0. Its interp now reads on at the first abscissa as numpy's does, and both engines reach 919.84 ohm-m over 0.7019 m. Perturbing Python's forward model by 1e-15 to 1e-10 moves its answer by at most 6.8e-8. The question the case was held open for stands for the owner as a product question, no longer one of parity: should the resolution the reports give (today the thickness factor only) cover a layer's resistivity too?
